newsitem.title: USA: USAir sees BA's plan to sell stake as first step.
newsitem.headline: USAir sees BA's plan to sell stake as first step.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said Wednesday British Airways Plc's plan to sell its stake in USAir was merely a "first step" in USAir's plan to regain independence.
"This is an important first step that USAir has been seeking in order for it to become an effective, independent competitor to London's Heathrow airport," USAir said in a statement.

Three years ago, BA gained a 24.6 percent stake in USAir and three seats on the airline's board in exchange for a much-needed $300 million capital infusion. BA later paid an additional $100 million to maintain its stake.
BA said Wednesday it was required to offer the shares to USAir before selling them to another party. Arlington, Va.-based USAir has 60 days to decide whether to repurchase the stake.
If USAir did not accept the offer, BA would be free to sell its stake by private transaction or by public offering.
BA also said its three directors on USAir's board would resign once the share sale was completed.
Both BA and USAir declined to disclose the price BA sought for the shares. USAir also declined to comment on whether it would buy the shares.
USAir further said it would "vigorously" pursue its lawsuit against BA and AMR Corp's American Airlines.
In July, USAir sued BA and American over their proposed marketing alliance.
USAir contended that the pact would undermine the existing relationship between USAir and BA and would allow BA and American to monopolize air travel between the United States and Britain.
USAir will end its code-sharing pact with BA on March 29.
